modules.title: Cardiology
modules.rationale: STEMI reperfusion and myocarditis are both 0%, and RV infarct versus posterior MI has been open since 14 August. Perioperative anticoagulation is excluded because the Anticoagulation module already covers it.

modules.title: Infectious Disease
modules.rationale: Antimicrobials sits at 0% and has been open since 16 August — the miss was assuming penicillin resistance in S. pyogenes. Built around empirical choice by syndrome under Australian guidelines, plus penicillin allergy, sepsis and the febrile returned traveller.

modules.title: Weak Areas — Round Two
modules.rationale: Second pass at the flagged failures, deliberately avoiding everything the first weak-areas module already teaches. Takes the next tier instead: cord localisation, third nerve palsy, raised intracranial pressure, the neuromuscular junction, and gout when NSAIDs are contraindicated.

modules.title: Gastroenterology
modules.rationale: Requested module. Cirrhosis complications and dysphagia both sit at 0%, and dysphagia has been missed as a discrimination failure in both directions, so the teaching is weighted to decompensated liver disease and to reading the onset pattern rather than the endpoint.

modules.title: Neurology
modules.rationale: Requested module, aimed at the tracked failures rather than the whole system: stroke at 0% (thrombolysis timing and posterior-circulation localisation), movement disorders 0%, nerve roots 0%, and head injury missed twice. Headache, seizures, demyelination and neuromuscular are at 100% and are left alone.

modules.title: Endocrine
modules.rationale: Requested module. Adrenal is your highest-volume weakness at 56% over 27 questions, so this covers the adrenal axis properly and then the rest of the system — thyroid, calcium and diabetes emergencies — which have barely been tested.

modules.title: Your Repeat Failures
modules.rationale: Built from the four errors your tracker shows you making repeatedly: Parkland missed 3 times with the identical wrong answer, ANZCOR adrenaline timing missed 4 times, periop bridging now wrong in both directions, and the primary-vs-secondary adrenal fork missed 5 times.

modules.title: Dermatology
modules.rationale: Requested module. Dermatology has notes but no test data at all — this converts an untested system into a measured one, weighted to the recognition patterns and emergencies that carry marks.

modules.title: The Adrenal Axis
modules.rationale: Your highest-volume weakness: 47% across 17 questions. The recorded misses show one principle failing repeatedly across three different diseases — renin direction misread in Addison's, Conn's, and renal artery stenosis.

modules.title: Anticoagulation
modules.rationale: Selected from your tracker: 0% across all three anticoagulation topics.
